760887.name: Time Pod [game_rule]
760887.text: The Time Pod is a special item in Into The Breach that can randomly drop during missions. Description: During each Mission, there is a chance for a pod to appear from the future, dropping it onto a random tile. This can happen in any Mission except for ones with the Protect the Corporate Tower objective. A new objective is added when this event happens: Protect the Time Pod. The 1st and 2nd islands in a timeline will always have one Time Pod. The 3rd and 4th island will always have two Time Pods. Note that this number also includes the appearance of a Strange Pod, which has a 15% chance of replacing a Time Pod in the 2nd, 3rd or 4th island. Protecting or rescuing the Pod always grants a Reactor Core. Time Pods may also contain a Pilot, a Weapon, or a piece of Passive equipment. If the Vek end on the tile where the Pod is, or if it takes damage from a Mech or a Vek attack, the Pod will be destroyed. Projectile weapons can pass safely over the pod, but not piercing/beam weapons. A Pod is still destroyed if the Vek who steps on it has Flying. If the Pod remains untouched until the end of the mission, it is recovered as well. Media:

761150.name: Smoke Tile [terrain]

Some weapons and enemy attacks are capable of creating their own Smoke Tiles as well. Units under Smoke will be denoted with the Smoke status, and will clear if the unit moves out of Smoke. If a unit is on Fire when it moves into a Smoke Tile, the fire will be put out. On the other hand, if a Smoke Tile is hit by an attack that does fire damage, the Smoke will be replaced by a Fire Tile.

760895.name: Corporate Reputation [game_rule]
760895.text: Corporate Reputation is one of the Resources in Into the Breach. Corporate Reputation Points are earned for successfully completing objectives during Missions. The Corporate Store becomes available after fighting the Hive Leader of an island. Corporate Reputation Points cannot be carried over to another island. Corporate Store: There are always 2-4 Weapons available at a cost of 2 Corporate Reputation. Reactor Cores can be bought for 3 Corporate Reputation each. Grid Power can be purchased for 1 Corporate Reputation each to repair the Power Grid or to Overpower Grid Defense. Weapons can be donated for 1 Corporate Reputation. Pilots can be donated for 1 Corporate Reputation, unless they have Popular Hero, in which case they will be donated for 4 instead.

760894.name: Grid Power [game_rule]
760894.text: Grid Power is reduced when Civilian Buildings are damaged. When it reaches zero, the player loses and the current run ends. The Power Grid indicator shows how much Grid Power remains. The player begins the game with 5 Grid Power and may have up to 7. If Grid Power would be increased beyond 7, Grid Defense increases instead. Increases and decreases to Grid Power persist between Islands. Gaining Grid Power: Grid Power can be regained by the following means: * Some missions grant Grid Power as a Resource reward for completing bonus objective(s). * *After finishing a Corporate Island, the player can buy 1 Grid Power for every 1 Corporate Reputation point spent. * *When completing a Perfect Island, the player can choose +2 Grid Power as their reward. * *The Grid Charger weapon, if found, restores 1 Grid Power when used successfully. (* On Unfair difficulty, this gain is doubled.) Grid Defense: Grid Defense is the percentage chance that a building tile will resist damage. Grid Defense starts at 15%. (On Unfair difficulty, Grid Defense starts at 0% but can still be increased.) Grid Defense can be increased by the following means: * Overpower Bonus. Each point of Grid Power obtained when the Power Grid is full increases Grid Defense by 2% (the first 5 times), then by 1%, up to a maximum of +25%. *Pilot Bonus. While equipped, a pilot with the +3 Grid DEF skill increases Grid Defense by that amount. With three pilots, this bonus can reach +9%. Combined, these bonuses can raise Grid Def

760869.name: Squads [game_rule]
760869.text: Squads in Into The Breach determine the Mechs you can take with you onto the battlefield. You start with the Rift Walkers squad. Additional squads are unlocked by completing Achievements. Each completed achivement earns 1 coin. Each squad has a custom paint job. Unlocked mech colors can be applied to other squads. Random Squads and Custom Squads: Once a second squad is acquired, the option to create a randomized squad or a customized squad opens up. A Custom Squad allows for the selection of any Mechs that have been unlocked, including multiple of the same class as well as multiple of the same Mech. A Random Squad is created out of all the unlocked Mechs. * The Balanced Roll option selects three unique Mechs from three of the five different classes (Prime, Brute, Ranged, Science, and Cyborg). The balanced squad won't have more than 4 weapons so this prevents the Flame Mech, Rocket Mech, Defense Mech, Gravity Mech, Nano Mech, Smog Mech, and Napalm Mech from appearing together in a balanced squad. * The Chaos Roll option has no restrictions on class, weaponry, or Mech combinations so you get a truly random squad. However, if you get duplicate Mechs with the same Passive ability, one of the duplicate Mechs will have the Passive and any power associated with it removed. Secret Squad: The Secret Squad becomes available after unlocking the 8 named squads. 25 Coins are required to unlock the Secret Squad. With the Advance Edition release, it is no longer needed to complete all Gl

760878.name: Vek [game_rule]
760878.text: The Vek are the main enemies encountered in Into The Breach. Gameplay: The main goal of Into the Breach is to make sure that the Vek do not destroy all of the grid power. Each island has a set variety of Vek that can spawn, one of which is a Psion, a supporting unit that grants a passive bonus to others. They emerge from the ground on certain tiles, which can be intercepted at the cost of 1 health during the enemy turn. Before the player turn any active Vek will move to a certain tile and prepare to attack it, aiming for either a mech, building or objective. These attacks are executed during the enemy turn unless they are cancelled or the Vek is killed beforehand. Vek are divided into five main groups: *Common Vek are those that can spawn on any island and make up most of the spawns on a mission. All of them have a soft limit on spawns per mission that can be bypassed if the spawning algorithm needs to. * Rare Vek are those whose attacks are more unique than common ones and do not appear on early islands. *Psions, which provide passive bonuses to other Vek when spawned. Note that the Psion itself does not benefit from the passive bonus. *Minor Vek, which are spawned by other Vek, are typically very weak, and bypass the spawning algorithm. They are not worth any experience and are not affected by Psion bonuses. *Hive Leaders, bosses found on the final mission of each island, the Volcanic Hive and normal missions on the fourth island in Unfair difficulty. Rare Vek and Psions ha

761012.name: Missions [game_rule]
761012.text: Missions are issued within each island you defend with your squads. Each mission has specific objectives, such as protecting or destroying certain units and buildings. Details: Missions are determined by the number of bonus objectives that can be fulfilled for either Corporate Reputation , Grid Power or Reactor Cores . A mission has at least one bonus objective and a maximum of three excluding newly-generated ones from a time pod. The number of objectives determines a sector's difficulty: * 1 objective: Defensive shields are placed on random buildings. These missions only have one objective, that gives out one power or reputation. * 2 objectives: No modifier applied. These missions either have two objectives, with each giving out one power, reputation or Reactor Core, or one objective that gives out two power or reputation. * 3 objectives: High-threat detected, meaning at least one alpha Vek and increased spawns. These missions can have up to three objectives, with the total rewards adding up to 3 of either Reactor Cores, power, or reputation. Usually a building that rewards a Reactor Core will be present. Time Pods can randomly appear in missions and require the player to protect it until the end of the mission or collect it using a mech or allied unit. They always reward a Reactor Core and have a chance of giving a weapon, passive or pilot. Upon landing a new objective called Protect the Time Pod will appear, which "rewards" the pod. A corporate island has five missions, fo

While alive, they grant all other Vek except for any Blobs, Spores, Spiderlings and Spiderling Eggs the ability to spawn a Spiderling Egg on death. The Spiderling Egg matches those that spawn from the Spider Leader and does not web surrounding tiles. 760936.name: Passives [game_rule]
760936.text: Passives are pieces of Mech equipment in Into the Breach. Description: Passives confer a constant benefit to all Mechs in the squad, without the need of activating them during an encounter. Since an action does not need to be used to activate passives, their effects will persist even when the Mech equipped with a passive is submerged into Water, a Lava Tile, an A.C.I.D. Tile, affected by Smoke, or even if the Mech is downed and disabled. Some Mechs come equipped with Passives by default. All Passives are treated as Any Class equipment, and can be equipped without penalty by any Mech Class (except Cyborg). Some Passives come with an upgrade or two, at the cost of additional Reactor Core usage. Upgrades are not purchased separately, they are included. Note that powering Upgrade 1 is never a prerequisite for powering Upgrade 2. Mechs with Passives in Custom Squads: When creating a Custom Squad, it is possible to choose a Mech which has a passive equipped multiple times. In this case, the duplicate Mechs will have the passive removed in their loadout, and only one Mech will keep the Passive for the Custom Squad. List:

Special: Burrower: This Vek will hide underground after taking one or more damage. | Stable : Cannot be moved by any weapon effect (Push, Teleport, etc.).. Burrowers move underground to arrive at their destination and bypass any obstacles, much like a Leaper minus the jumping. When emerging they attack a 3-tile wide area in front of them perpendicular to where they are facing. Upon taking any damage, they will cancel their attack and retreat underground, re-emerging elsewhere (within 4 tiles of where they retreated from) on their next turn. Burrowers can not end their move on top of Ice Tiles. Burrowers are Stable and thus cannot be pushed or moved with physical force, however they can still be relocated by the Control Mech's Control Shot weapon.
